_comment: AP Networking topic to industry certification crosswalk.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
College Board's own framing for AP Networking is that it was developed with
industry partners including Cisco and aligns to CompTIA Network+, Cisco CCNA
and Cisco CCST Networking. As of the 2026-08-17 depth audit, zero of the 22
published topic pages mentioned any of them. That is the largest gap in the
course AND the only one that cannot be invalidated by a CED revision, because
certification objectives are published, stable, and owned by someone else.
It is also the argument that reaches an administrator rather than a student.
'Aligned to AP' is a sentence. 'Aligned to AP and maps to Network+ and CCST'
is a budget line.
MAPPING GRANULARITY, AND WHY IT STOPS WHERE IT DOES
This maps at DOMAIN level, not sub-objective level. Domain names and the
Network+ weightings were corroborated across multiple independent sources.
Sub-objective numbers (for example 'N10-009 2.1') live in the official
blueprints on comptia.org and cisco.com, both of which are blocked by this
environment's egress proxy, so they could not be read first-hand.
Publishing a sub-objective number sourced from a third-party summary would be
the same failure the AP Networking hazard block already forbids: a wrong
identifier is worse than an absent one, because it gets quoted onward as if
it were checked. Domain level is what could be verified, so domain level is
what ships. See docs/ap-networking-cert-crosswalk.md to deepen it later.
PRIMARY vs SECONDARY
primary   the domain a teacher would name if asked what this topic is for
secondary genuinely covered, but not the topic's centre of gravity
Every claim is deliberately conservative. Over-claiming coverage is how a
crosswalk stops being trusted.

comptia_network_plus.note: Five domains with published weightings. Weightings corroborated across multiple independent summaries.
comptia_network_plus.official_blueprint: https://www.comptia.org (blocked by this environment's egress proxy, not read first-hand)

cisco_ccst_networking.note: Six domains. Cisco does not publish per-domain percentage weightings for this exam, so none are claimed here.
cisco_ccst_networking.official_blueprint: https://www.cisco.com (blocked by this environment's egress proxy, not read first-hand)

cisco_ccna.note: Named in College Board's alignment statement but deliberately NOT mapped here. CCNA is a professional-level exam well beyond a first-year high school course, and claiming topic-level alignment to it would be the kind of over-claim that gets a crosswalk dismissed. It is mentioned in prose as the onward path, not mapped as coverage.

topics.title: Troubleshooting issues on my device
topics.note: The course opens on the same skill Network+ weights most heavily. Worth saying out loud on the page.

topics.title: Connecting and optimizing my device
topics.note: Secure wireless connectivity sits in both the implementation and security halves of Network+.

topics.title: MAC and IP addresses
topics.note: The clearest one-to-one match in the course. CCST devotes an entire domain to it.

topics.title: Adding a media server and AI devices to the network
Switching and network topologies
topics.note: Topologies are named explicitly in the CCST standards domain.

topics.title: Configuring and verifying access
topics.note: The topic with the most uncited EK codes in the depth audit, and the one that reaches the most cert domains. Worth authoring first.

topics.title: Network failures and the CIA triad
topics.note: CIA is named directly in the CCST security domain.

topics.title: Protocols and the OSI and TCP/IP models
topics.note: Network+ objective 1.1 is the OSI model. This topic is as close to a direct hit as the course gets.

topics.title: Monitoring and defending the network
topics.note: The only topic whose primary Network+ domain is Operations, which is 19 percent of that exam and otherwise thin across this course.
